issues.description: Tests pass a bogus zero-amount/zero-puzhash Addition to bypass the non-empty additions invariant
issues.detail: Tests substitute additions=[] with Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros) to satisfy CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__'s len(additions)<1 check. The production cat_spend path branches on additions is not None but the forwarded payload still requires a non-empty list. The test was bent to fit the code path; fix the data model, not the tests.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction becomes a junk drawer of CAT- and decorator-specific optional fields with no mutual-exclusivity validation
issues.detail: extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution, and puzzle_decorator are now first-class fields on a general endpoint type with no __post_init__ check ensuring CAT fields only apply to CAT wallets. The type admits nonsensical states (XCH send with tail_reveal set). Extract a CatDiscrepancy value object and pass it through, or add explicit invariants.

issues.description: Address-prefix validation semantics silently changed from network-config string compare to AddressType.XCH enum membership
issues.detail: Old send_transaction rejected addresses whose bech32 prefix didn't match the network config's address_prefix. New code uses ensure_valid_address(allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}), a different check. On testnet/simulator builds where the configured prefix is not xch, this is a behavior change and possibly a regression. Pin the error contract with a test or restore the original check.

issues.description: puzzle_decorator handling diverges silently between send_transaction and cat_spend
issues.detail: Old send_transaction forwarded only request.puzzle_decorator[0]; new code passes the whole list, changing observable behavior for callers sending more than one entry. Meanwhile cat_spend builds CreateSignedTransaction without forwarding request.puzzle_decorator at all, despite CATSpend accepting it. Two endpoints, two different silent semantic changes — pick one contract.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation extracted with its bad-taste set-membership trick and type-ignores intact
issues.detail: The helper uses None in {extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution} with three # type: ignore[arg-type] comments. An explicit if any(x is None for x in (...)) narrows properly, removes the ignores, and reads as the intended invariant. Moving bad taste into a function makes it reusable bad taste; clean it up while extracting.

issues.description: Discarded get_wallet result with '# opportunity to raise' comment hides validation intent
issues.detail: Calling get_wallet purely for its raising side effect with a comment acknowledging it is a code smell. Extract a named _validate_wallet_type(wallet_id, required_type) helper whose name states the intent, so the next reader doesn't stumble over an apparently-unused call.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the deduplication idea — send_transaction and cat_spend as thin wrappers over create_signed_transaction — is the right shape, but the execution leaks invariants. The clearest signal is that tests had to invent a zero-amount/zero-puzhash Addition to satisfy the non-empty-list guard, which means the data model doesn't fit the wrapped call. Two unannounced behavior changes slipped in: puzzle_decorator handling now diverges between endpoints, and address-prefix validation switched from network-config string compare to AddressType.XCH enum membership. The widened CreateSignedTransaction admits nonsensical CAT/XCH combinations without validation, and the extracted cat_discrepancy_validation carries forward its type-ignores and set-membership trick instead of being cleaned up. Needs-work: fix the additions model, pin the semantic changes, and split into reviewable patches.
